notes: Clicked for credits nearly every turn up to 59 credits with nothing to spend them on, never ran HQ or R&D, and kept rerunning the remote to see the same declined Obokata. Let the Corp score three agendas without contesting them, then wasted the final turns clearing tags off IP Block.

Scored steadily from a one-ice remote and won, but left HQ and R&D open early (two agendas stolen from HQ on turn 1). Several turns of clicking for credits and pointless ambush rezzes, though a passive Runner hid most of the mistakes.

Reached 6 points by turn 4 and then stopped running for 15 turns, clicking for credits up to 45 while needing one agenda, and MaxX milled the stack to empty. Early turns also repeated HQ runs that saw cards already seen.
Built a deep remote and scored out cleanly with Hedge Funds and Seamless Launch. An early Cyberdex Sandbox behind one ice was stolen, and there were a few idle credit-click turns.

Kept piling up tags from Liza, so the Corp trashed resources every turn; paid 4 net damage to steal Obokata and then ran HQ through Kakugo down to 0 cards. Ran Kakugo again with an empty grip and flatlined, a foreseeable loss at 6 points.
Built a four-ice remote and then never installed an agenda in it, clicking for credits up to 28 while discarding from a full HQ. Agendas sat in HQ behind one Gatekeeper and were stolen there.
Good Information Sifting dig on HQ for 5 points on turn 1, then steady R&D and HQ pressure past a non-ETR Architect won on turn 4. There were only minor inefficiencies.
After taking 4 points from Archives, clicked for credits for about 12 straight turns (up to 49) without running while the Corp scored from fresh remotes. MaxX milled the stack out, leaving no plan.

Spent turns 2-5 clicking for credits and discarding with no remote or R&D ice, then put agendas into a one-ice remote where three were stolen. The win came from Fairchild core damage against a broke Runner, not from a plan.
Fast and effective: scored repeatedly behind IP Block while the Runner was locked out, with good use of Hedge Fund and Biotic Labor. HQ and R&D stayed unprotected far too long, but that cost little.

Won quickly by scoring from the Fairchild remote and fast-advancing, but ran very low on credits. Pointlessly used Élivágar to derez its own Fairchild and left R&D ice unrezzed while agendas were stolen from it.

Won by taking 4 points from Archives after Audacity and then hitting HQ and R&D steadily. Facechecked Border Control without a breaker early and left 2 tags up, which let High-Profile Target wipe Paperclip and the hand.

Advanced Global Food Initiative in a remote with no ice and lost it, then played Audacity to dump two agendas into open Archives for 5 Runner points. Fairchild core damage rescued the game, and there were many idle credit clicks.
Hoarded 56 credits by clicking and then ran Archives 16 times to see the same declined Obokata. Never ran HQ, R&D or the scoring remotes, so the Corp scored every agenda unopposed.

Good HQ and R&D pressure, with well-timed net-damage Obokata steals and a quick Send a Message steal. It wasted credits paying Engolo before an Ika break and took some clumsy draw turns, but won comfortably.

Clicked for credits nearly every turn up to 32 with a full HQ and never added real ice to HQ or the remote. Let Drafter install agendas into a remote guarded only by Drafter, where GFI, Offworld and Luminal were stolen.
Aggressive R&D runs and an Archives check after Audacity won on turn 3. It could have checked Archives a turn earlier, right after the Corp's mass trash.

Spent much of the game at 0-3 credits and clicking for credits, and kept a single Pup on R&D and a single Eli on HQ for 30 turns. Fetal AI was stolen from a one-ice remote, but Mushin traps and scoring Gila/House of Knives showed some plan.
Scored three agendas efficiently with Seamless Launch from Gatekeeper and Border Control remotes. There were a couple of idle credit-click turns with a full HQ.

Ran an unchanged R&D four times per turn and HQ repeatedly with no gain, then clicked for credits for six turns while the Corp installed and scored agendas from a lightly iced remote. Contested only the final agenda, too late.
